messages:
alex: Heads-up — Seawall cutover is scheduled for TOMORROW 09:00 PT. During the dry-run we noticed audit logs aren't arriving in the customer's Splunk cluster. Can infra/security owners triage? @dinesh @sara :warning:

maria: Thanks for flagging. Is this only audit logs or also request logs? Any error samples from forwarding?

dinesh: Quick summary: forwarding is configured via our logging lambda -> KMS-encrypted S3 -> Splunk forwarder. When I ran the test put-object we got a KMS "AccessDenied" on Encrypt response. Looks like the KMS key policy denies aws:SourceAccount for the customer's account id. Repro snippet here:

```
aws s3 cp test.json s3://seawall-logs-test/ --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abc-123
An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the PutObject operation: Access Denied
```

We also see CloudTrail entries: kms:GenerateDataKey -> AccessDenied.

sara: That's likely the root cause. If the key policy is too restrictive the Splunk ingestor (or our cross-account role) can't decrypt. This is a compliance risk for the customer's audit retention SLA — if we don't get logs in the retention window it's a renewal/ops risk.

alex: Can we get an ETA? Customer success needs to message the customer if we hit delay. Also we should have a short mitigation we can offer in the meantime.

maria: I can draft the customer message once we have an ETA and mitigation. Suggested temporary mitigation: switch to a Redwood-managed key with explicit cross-account allow while we fix customer's key policy. Would need security signoff.

dinesh: Plan: 1) Confirm key policy clause blocking SourceAccount 2) Propose minimal policy patch to allow our forwarder role 3) Test end-to-end in staging 4) Roll change to prod. I can take ownership for steps 1–3. ETA: 90 mins to verify + patch in staging, 3 hours for full prod roll pending approval.

sara: SGTM. Important constraints: must not widen key access beyond the specific IAM principal and kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt for that use-case. I'll review the policy change. If we do managed-key fallback, security needs a short-lived allow with strict principal and expiration.

alex: @dinesh please post the minimal policy snippet when you have it. @maria hold off on customer comms until we have the staging test green — but prepare the message template. Use this runbook link: https://redwood-internal/onboard/seawall (attach if they ask).

dinesh: Pasting proposed minimal policy (will validate with sara):

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodForwarder",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDWOOD_ACCOUNT:role/log-forwarder"},
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:SourceArn": "arn:aws:s3:::seawall-logs-*"}}
    }
  ]
}
```

I'll test in staging in ~30m.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: logging-forwarder/staging config update (job 8921). ETA ~20m.

maria: Drafted message snippet for CS Slack to customer (will personalize after staging pass): "Quick update: During a pre-cutover dry-run we observed encryption permissions on your KMS key preventing log forwarding. We're applying a minimal update to allow Redwood's forwarder role to write encrypted logs; this is low-risk and reversible. We'll confirm end-to-end and share a status update within 3 hours. If you'd prefer, we can temporarily switch to a Redwood-managed key while we complete validation."

alex: Nice. Sara when you finish your review can you thumbs-up or suggest edits here? we need explicit signoff to proceed. :thumbsup:

sara: Reviewing now. Two quick asks: add aws:SourceAccount = 123456789012 condition (tighten by account) and set a patch window <2 hours. Otherwise LGTM.

dinesh: Added SourceAccount condition and pinned expiration to 2h in the staging temp key policy. Running tests now. Will post results.

deploy-bot: Deployment succeeded: logging-forwarder/staging config update (job 8921). Tests kicked off.

dinesh: Staging tests: put-object succeeded, CloudTrail shows successful GenerateDataKey and PutObject. End-to-end looks green. Pushing a request for Sara's prod signoff.

sara: Prod policy approved with SourceAccount + principal restriction. Proceed with prod patch during the maintenance window (rolling, no downtime).

alex: Excellent. Maria — go ahead and send updated customer note: 1) root cause 2) mitigation applied 3) expected prod patch time + CTA if they want managed-key fallback. Keep tone reassuring.

maria: Will send now and follow up after prod patch.

alex: Thanks team. I'll mark this as owner:dinesh, blocker:resolved-in-staging, next: prod-roll (ETA 2h). :white_check_mark:
